_about: The studio-show REGISTRY: one entry per show docs/research/studio-shows.md verified with a 2026 slot. pipeline/load_studio_shows.py reads this, upserts `studio_shows`, and generates one `studio_show` program per air date. SCOPE is register section 7 Q4: pregame and postgame BOOKENDS on the game's network - no halftime, no daily talk. A studio show never gets a chip (section 9); it renders under the sport it covers.

_not_loaded.why: the doc gives 'Thu ~7:00 PM ET' - with the tilde - and marks the 2026 roster UNVERIFIED. An approximate start is not a slot; a program placed on the grid at a guessed minute is a broadcast fact this run does not invent.
five games in 2026, only one of them dated in the doc (Melbourne, Thu Sept 10), and 'pregame format [UNVERIFIED]'. No slot, no duration, no network row that can be generated per air date.

_not_loaded.show: NASCAR RaceDay (FOX) and the USA Sports pre/post-race shows
_not_loaded.why: the doc gives the USA shows as '30 min each side of the race' but states NO start time for RaceDay and no source that machine-reads either. The pre/post pair could be DERIVED from each race's start - and deriving a broadcast from another broadcast is a rule the research has not blessed, so it waits for nascar.com/tv-schedule to be verified (docs/research/nascar.md section 6 marks it UNVERIFIED).

_findings.result: CLEAN, and it carries more than the doc promised. The Week 1 release gives College GameDay's site (Baton Rouge, Louisiana), its window (Sat Sept 5, 9 a.m. to noon ET), its networks (ESPN, ESPNU, Disney+, the ESPN App) AND its ANNOUNCED nine-member 2026 on-air team. That is an announcement, which is a better source than the hand-curation register section 17 permits.
200, but its single table is a HISTORICAL January bowl-season table, not the weekly Date/Site/Game table. The weekly site lives in each week's own release.

200 on every path tried - /presspass, /presspass/latest-news and /presspass/latest-news/weekly-schedule - and ZERO tables and zero occurrences of 'Big Noon' in any of them. The doc marked fetchability UNVERIFIED; it is now verified as fetch-clean but CONTENT-EMPTY, because the page is JS-rendered. So Big Noon's site is `tba` and is never guessed.
